Kestrel Computer Project: Aiming to build a full-stack, open source, and open hardware home computer

Seems interesting, and a claim it makes is

The Kestrel-4 will target financial, insurance, medical, nuclear reclaimation, weather prediction, enterprise file serving, enterprise web cache applications...

But what worries me is this:

Kestrel Forth V4.0 will introduce support for virtual partitions (VPARs), running Linux applications as Forth words.

So if I wanted to run a tomcat web app, I'd have to run my web container in a JVM running as a linux app in a Forth word? I'm curious if there are any kind of idiosyncrasies that'd crop up in trying to get such an application working in that environment. And then there's sure to be a performance hit you'd take. I'd love it if someone had experience in using Forth for this kind of work and could shed some light.

Forth isn't exactly bursting with popularity nor is it a flavor-of-the-month language, so I see this project having a difficult time attracting early adopters. I'm rooting for it though; we need more technology like this as a choice over close-source proprietary software and hardware stacks where telemetry, backdoors, and patent lawsuits increasingly continue to rule the day.

Disgaea series is an addicting series

I ADORE Disgaea. Discovered it on my PSP, last game was Disgaea 3 on my PS Vita.

My best memory of Disgaea, though, isn't technically Disgaea related, and I hope you'll excuse the tangent. I was a huge Tribes: Ascend player when it still had hope and Hi-Rez actually gave a shit about it, and was pretty damn good at it too. I started experimenting with underused weapons and classes to have fun. With the release of a map called Raindance, things got broken. I created an impenetrable defense on a capture the flag map with only one entrance. Frag mines lining the entrance, force fields that do damage, and a heavy bolt launcher that, when all combined, was a death trap. I'd listen for a hit marker for one of the mines, shift my attention to the game, click, enjoy free kill. Wait until my team wins the game, enjoy the huge amount of unlock credits for more stuff while being at the top of the board.

This got so easy that I started to wonder how hard I could AFK it. I'd alt-tab and browse the internet, but that was easy. How far could I take it? Oh, I know! Why not play Disgaea 3? So I pulled the Vita out of the drawer, threw in the game cartridge, and started playing. It was surprising how much I could do before people could get to my defenses, and at the same time acquire enough points to dominate every game on that map. It was so fucking awesome being able to play Disgaea while just listening for a damage sound from one of my mines. Eventually the strategy got so popular that they had to change the map to make easier to assault the enemy's base. Those were some good fucking times.
